task_instance: Given a sample Zscaler ZIA export (URL filtering rules, locations, users/groups CSVs), build an inventory, apply the skill's mapping heuristics, and produce a full Cloudflare One migration mapping plan plus an assessment document following the skill's template, accounting for every source rule (migrated / partial / not-migrated) and passing the object-count validation gate.
evidence: Created sample_export/{url_filtering_rules.csv, locations.csv, users_groups.csv} representing a minimal ZIA export. Wrote build_mapping.py which parses the export and applies the skill's mapping heuristics (BLOCK/ALLOW -> Gateway HTTP policy; CAUTION -> flagged manual_review with no exact equivalent; group rules without SCIM -> needs_identity prerequisite; disabled/0-hit rules -> Not Migrated candidate; locations -> source IP lists, not auto DNS locations; GRE tunnel -> separate WARP/WAN workstream note). Ran `python3 build_mapping.py`, producing mapping_plan.json with a validation block showing source_rule_count=6, mapped_high_confidence=5, manual_review_required=1, flagged_not_migrated=1, passed=true (6 source rules all accounted for in 6 output rows, satisfying the skill's 'account for every source rule' and 'compare object counts, stop on mismatch' requirements). Wrote migration_assessment.md following the skill's exact Assessment Template (Source stack, Artifacts reviewed, Assumptions, Recommended target, Mapping summary table, Risks/partial mappings, Not migrated, Pilot plan, Validation, Rollback). Verified all 6 source rules and both locations appear in the mapping tables with confidence levels and a rollback/pilot plan present. This is the skill's core deliverable (an assessment/mapping plan for VPN/SASE-to-Cloudflare-One migration); it does not require a live Cloudflare account, API keys, or provisioning against Cloudflare's control plane, so it was fully achievable in this sandbox without credentials.
